reasons: internal/httpapi/tracking_handlers.go:261-292 (proxyMomento/momentoProxyPath) still forwards every path under the collector base: the fix only refuses '..'/'.'/'//' segments, so /momento/<anything> is relayed to <momento_url>/<anything> for GET/HEAD/POST/OPTIONS with the visitor's query and body. The documented and UI-placeholder value for tracking.momento_url is an origin with no base path (https://momento.internal), which makes '<momento_url>/*' the entire internal collector host: an anonymous visitor can reach the collector's dashboard, admin/API, login, health or OIDC endpoints through Qurio (Cookie/Authorization are stripped inbound and Set-Cookie outbound, but unauthenticated collector routes and token-in-body logins are fully reachable). The campaign rule (DartFly/qurio/ptium, 3 hits) requires the same-origin proxy to pass only the collector endpoints the snippet uses. Fix: allow-list the exact requests the injected snippet makes — GET/HEAD /momento/tracker.js and POST to the Momento contract-v1 events endpoint(s) that data-endpoint="/momento" resolves to (the tests already assume /collect/v1/events; confirm against Momento's tracker.js for data-contract-version="1") — answer 404 for everything else (including /momento/, /momento/api/..., /momento/admin, and OPTIONS which is unnecessary same-origin), and extend TestMomentoProxyStaysUnderCollectorBase so that /momento/, /momento/api/x and /momento/admin/x with momento_url set to a bare origin are asserted 404 while tracker.js and the events POST still reach the upstream. If the Momento request contract cannot be determined from available sources, escalate to human instead of guessing.
notes: The three items from the previous rejection are otherwise addressed and verified: '..'/encoded traversal is refused (TestMomentoProxyStaysUnderCollectorBase fails with 200 when the path.Clean check is removed, passes with it); handleAllowTrackingHost now uses readTrackingConfig, refuses on read failure (503, TestAllowTrackingHostRefusesToBuildOnFailedRead) and serialises read-modify-write with allowedHostsMu; trackingAllowedHosts is registered in settingSpecs so both PUT /admin/settings and POST /admin/tracking/allow run it, and it rejects 'unsafe-inline', *, data:, https:, bare hosts, paths, userinfo and bad ports (TestTrackingSettingsValidation).

go build/vet/test for internal/tracking and internal/httpapi pass (-count=1). Frontend vitest (web/src/pages/AdminPages.test.ts) could not be run in this checkout (no node_modules); the rebuilt internal/webui/dist assets were not verified against source.

Defaults are off on a fresh install (tracking.enabled=false, provider=none; TestFreshInstallationServesUntouchedShellWithStrictPolicy asserts identical shell and base CSP). Non-blocking: POST /api/v1/tracking/csp-report is unauthenticated by necessity but accepts reports regardless of whether tracking is active, so anyone can plant an arbitrary origin in the 차단된 출처 table and invite an administrator to click 허용 on it. Consider ignoring reports while no tracking config is active and/or labelling the table as untrusted browser input.

Non-blocking: httputil.ReverseProxy is built per request (it shares http.DefaultTransport, so no connection/goroutine leak, but the campaign rule prefers building it once).
